label: ε, x̂₀ and velocity: three ways to say the same thing
context: Draw one clean data point x_0 (blue dot, label 'x₀ data') at left and one noise sample ε (grey dot, label 'ε noise') at right, and the noisy point x_t on the straight line between them for the rectified-flow path x_t = (1 - t) x_0 + t ε; t moves slowly back and forth between 0.15 and 0.85, shown on a small t slider. From x_t draw three arrows in different colours and cycle a highlight through them with captions: (1) 'ε-prediction (DDPM, SD 1): where did the noise come from?' arrow toward ε; (2) 'x̂₀-prediction (AlphaFold 3, EDM): where is the data?' arrow toward x_0; (3) 'velocity v = ε − x₀ (SD3, FLUX): which way along the path?' arrow parallel to the line. End with all three shown and caption 'given x_t and t, any one determines the other two'. Canvas is responsive: width anywhere from 340 to 900 px, height 400 px; derive every size and position from width and height, keep all text at least 11 px and fully inside the canvas, and on narrow widths stack or shrink rather than overlap. Loop forever on a cycle of 10 to 16 s with smooth easing between phases. White background. Put a one-line phase caption at the top centre that changes with the phase. No title inside the canvas (the card has one). Use plain sans-serif labels.

spec.title: ε, x̂₀ and velocity: three ways to say the same thing
spec.caption: On the rectified-flow path xₜ = (1 − t) x₀ + t ε, predicting the noise ε, the clean data x̂₀ or the velocity v = ε − x₀ are interchangeable: given xₜ and t, any one determines the other two.
